what: Rain and snow seen falling in the ground battle (release 2, the look bible's G10; behind -TheaterLandFalling). Read by Effects/WeatherFall (FWeatherFall::LoadRecipe) for the falling drops ('fall') and by Battle/LandWeather for what falls over a battle and how the day changes for it ('pick' and 'day'). Every number has its standing value in the code (WeatherFall::Recipe::Standing, LandWeather.cpp): a number left out of this file keeps it, so this file is the art director's to tune without a code change. -TheaterFxSet=fall.rain.near.density=0.8 sets one over the file's at launch, as battle-fx.json's.

pick._how: What falls, from the battle's one weather draw (no new draw): the campaign's word over the place and the day's sky as drawn (the ticket's sky: rain a deck of 0.75 to 0.95, snow 0.8 to 1, mud 0.6 to 0.8). Strengths 0 to 1: light rain about 0.3, a downpour 1. Where snow lies (snow_lying_from and more), what falls is snow.

rain._how: always falls: least at from_cover, a downpour at full_cover; the jungle's, the islands' and rice country's heavier (tropic_more added), the desert's and the dry steppe's lighter (dry_times)

snow._how: the snow months: falls only under a deck of from_cover or more (about half their battles), least there, heaviest at full_cover

mud._how: the thaw and the autumn rains: a drizzle under the heaviest of their decks (from_cover and more)

day._how: How the day changes for it. The haze: its density times 1 + haze_more x strength (rain: x strength to the power haze_curve), its colour drawn haze_toward x strength (rain: x the strength's square root, so even a light rain's sky goes grey) of the way to haze_r, haze_g, haze_b (linear). The day's lamps times 1 - dimmer x strength; the sky's own brightness times 1 - sky_dimmer x strength (a grey lid darker than a dry overcast, and darker than the snow under it: the art director's R1 and S2). The open ground's wetness wet_least + (1 - wet_least) x strength; the ground's, the hedges' and things' and the steel's roughness and specular when wet (the dry ones: ground 0.95 and 0.15, things 0.9 and 0.2, steel 0.6 and 0.35). The drops' colour: the haze's times ink_over_haze.

fall._how: The drops, in layers about the eye, each a box (box_m a side) that goes where the eye goes, the drops in it staying put in the world while near: density a cubic metre at full strength (a strength shows that share of them), fall m/s (each drop its own, within spread of it either way), wind_share of the wind, width_m across (a flake's size), length_m long (rain's streak), alpha the most one shows, tone its colour's share of the ink; none nearer the lens than near_from_m, whole from near_full_m, fading from far_fade of half the box to its edge; flutter_m a flake's sway either way; order its place among the see-through things (near over the smoke, far under it); off 1 leaves a layer out. Every fall and wind is a whole number of rain_step (snow_step) m/s, so each layer comes round exactly. Nothing is drawn thinner than least_px pixels (its light kept). At no strength the drops show strength_alpha of their alpha and a streak strength_length of its length (a light rain's streaks shorter and fainter, a downpour's long). most_drops: a layer's mesh at most. Heavy rain at full strength: some 1,800 streaks in a 70 degree picture, covering about a sixth of it; heavy snow some 1,800 flakes (Tools/land_weather counts them). The far layers cost the most drops (about 52,000 each, of which about one in thirty is in the picture): fall.rain.far.density halves them, at a cost in the far grain.
